resources.string: The name of the app. It is a brand name: keep it as is, or transliterate it into your script only if that is the usual practice in your language.
Accessibility label for the button that opens the navigation (hamburger) menu.
Line at the top of the navigation menu. Parameter 1 is the Wikimedia username of the signed-in user.
Accessibility label for the top-bar button that resets the current recording session and returns to the first step (choosing a speaker profile).
Title of the confirmation dialog shown before resetting the current session.
Body text of the confirmation dialog shown before resetting the current session.
Button in the reset-session confirmation dialog that confirms the reset.
Button in the reset-session confirmation dialog that cancels the reset and returns to the session.
Small lowercase tagline above the sign-in screen headline, summarizing the three things the app does. The dots are separators.
Main pitch on the sign-in screen, explaining why recording pronunciations is useful.
Small lowercase heading on the sign-in screen, above a list of things the user needs.
The list of things the user needs before starting, shown under the heading \'you will need\'. The dots are separators.
Main button on the sign-in screen. Opens the Wikimedia login page in the browser.
Replaces the sign-in button text while signing in is in progress.
Reassurance note under the sign-in button: the login is done on the Wikimedia website (OAuth), so the app never handles the password.
Notice on the sign-in screen after the user was logged out (for example because their login expired).
Link on the sign-in screen that opens the Wikimedia account creation page.
Name of the language-selection screen, used in navigation. Refers to the language the user will record in, not the interface language.
Small heading on the language-selection screen: this is the second of the four steps for setting up a recording session.
Headline on the language-selection screen, asking which language the user will record words in.
Explanation under the language-selection headline. Parameter 1 is the name of the chosen speaker profile (a Wikimedia username).
Name of the screen where the user chooses where the list of words to record comes from, used in navigation.
Name of the recording screen, used in navigation. A noun: the act of recording.
Name of the screen where the user listens back to their recordings, used in navigation.
Name of the screen that uploads recordings to Wikimedia Commons and Wikidata, used in navigation.
Name of the Settings screen, used in the navigation menu.
Name of the statistics screen (how many recordings the user has made), used in the navigation menu.
Name of the About screen (version, license, credits), used in the navigation menu.
Small heading on the profile-selection screen: this is the first of the four steps for setting up a recording session. \'Speaker\' is the person who will be recorded.
Headline on the profile-selection screen, asking who will be recorded.
Explanation of what a speaker profile is, under the profile-selection headline.
Small lowercase line on each profile card, naming the two wikis the profile contributes to (Wikimedia Commons and Wikidata). The dot is a separator.
Button that opens the form for creating a new speaker profile.
Note at the bottom of the profile-selection screen.
Title of the confirmation dialog shown before deleting a speaker profile.
Body of the confirmation dialog shown before deleting a speaker profile. Parameter 1 is the name of the profile (a Wikimedia username).
Button in the delete-profile dialog that confirms deletion.
Button in the delete-profile dialog that cancels deletion.
Lowercase label on a profile card, next to a language the speaker speaks natively (as a mother tongue).
Lowercase label on a profile card, next to a language the speaker speaks well but not natively.
Option (capitalized) for choosing how well the speaker speaks a language: natively, as a mother tongue.
Option (capitalized) for choosing how well the speaker speaks a language: well, but not natively.
Lowercase label shown instead of a dialect name when the speaker records the standard form of a language (no particular dialect or region).
Generic Back button, returning to the previous screen.
Generic Cancel button.
Generic Add button, for example to add a language to a profile.
Title of the screen for creating a new speaker profile.
Label of the field showing the Wikimedia account username of the new profile.
Small tag next to the username, showing that the account was confirmed by signing in.
Label of an optional field for the name of the person being recorded, when that is not the account owner.
Explanation under the optional speaker name field.
Heading above the list of languages the speaker can record in.
Explanation under the languages heading on the new-profile screen.
Button that opens a dialog for adding one more language to the profile.
Note at the bottom of the new-profile screen, explaining why proficiency and dialect are asked for.
Button that saves the new speaker profile.
Accessibility label for the button that removes a language from the profile. Parameter 1 is the language name.
Title of the dialog for adding a language to a speaker profile.
Label of the field for searching and choosing a language by name.
Label of the field showing the ISO 639 code of the chosen language (for example \'en\' or \'he\').
Label above the choice between native and proficient.
Label of the optional field for a dialect or regional variety of the language.
Small heading: this is the third of the four steps for setting up a recording session, where the user chooses the list of words to record.
Headline on the screen for choosing where the list of words to record comes from.
Explanation under the list-source headline.
Small lowercase tag on the card for typing or pasting your own list of words.
Title of the card for typing or pasting your own list of words.
Description on the card for typing or pasting your own list. \'Item labels\' are names of Wikidata items (things, places, people); \'lexemes\' are Wikidata dictionary entries (words).
Small lowercase tag on the card for using a Wikidata SPARQL query. SPARQL is the name of a query language; usually left untranslated.
Title of the card for getting the list of words from a Wikidata SPARQL query.
Description on the card for using a Wikidata SPARQL query.
Small lowercase tag on the card for getting the list of words from a Wikipedia category.
Title of the card for getting the list of words from a Wikipedia category.
Description on the card for using a Wikipedia category.
Button that opens Recovery mode: a tool that finds the user\'s past uploads that were never linked from Wikidata and links them.
Note under the Recovery mode button, explaining when to use it.
Small heading on the Recovery mode screen.
Headline on the Recovery mode screen. \'Re-link\' means adding the missing links from Wikidata to recordings already on Commons.
Explanation of what Recovery mode does.
Label of the field for how many recent uploads to check. Parameter 1 is the maximum allowed number.
Button that starts checking the user\'s recent uploads.
Headline shown while Recovery mode is running.
Progress stage in Recovery mode: fetching the list of the user\'s recent Commons uploads.
Progress stage in Recovery mode: checking Wikidata for existing links to each recording.
Progress stage in Recovery mode: adding the missing links on Wikidata.
Headline shown when Recovery mode could not run (for example, no connection).
Headline shown when Recovery mode has finished.
Row label in the Recovery mode results table; a number is shown before it. Counts how many uploads were checked.
Row label in the Recovery mode results table; a number is shown before it. Counts how many of the checked uploads are recordings made with this app.
Row label in the Recovery mode results table; a number is shown before it. Counts recordings that were already linked from Wikidata.
Row label in the Recovery mode results table; a number is shown before it. Counts links newly added on Wikidata.
Row label in the Recovery mode results table; a number is shown before it. Counts links that could not be added because of an error.
Row label in the Recovery mode results table; a number is shown before it. Counts recordings for which the app could not work out which Wikidata item or lexeme form they belong to.
Small heading above the per-recording list of Recovery mode results.
Shown when none of the checked uploads were made with this app.
Short status tag on a recording in the Recovery mode results: it was already linked from Wikidata.
Short status tag on a recording in the Recovery mode results: the missing link was added.
Short status tag on a recording in the Recovery mode results: adding the link failed.
Short status tag on a recording in the Recovery mode results: the app could not tell where to link it.
Button that runs the Recovery mode check again.
Lowercase name of the list source, inserted as parameter 1 into the step heading \'Step 3 of 4 — ...\'. Refers to a list the user typed or pasted.
Name of the list source, inserted as parameter 1 into the step heading \'Step 3 of 4 — ...\'.
Name of the list source, inserted as parameter 1 into the step heading \'Step 3 of 4 — ...\'.

Small heading on the screen where the user fills in the chosen list source. Parameter 1 is the name of the source: \'your own list\', \'Wikidata query\' or \'Wikipedia category\' (translated separately).
Headline on the screen for typing or pasting your own list of words.
Headline on the screen for pasting a Wikidata SPARQL query.
Headline on the screen for entering a Wikipedia category name.
Label of the text box for typing or pasting the words, one per line.
Label of the text box for the SPARQL query. \'?item\' and \'?lexeme\' are SPARQL variable names and must not be translated.
Label of a menu of ready-made Wikidata queries the user can start from.
Ready-made query: all lexemes (Wikidata dictionary entries) in the chosen language.
Ready-made query: all nouns in the chosen language.
Ready-made query: all verbs in the chosen language.
Ready-made query: all adjectives in the chosen language.
Ready-made query: all adverbs in the chosen language.
Ready-made query: all phrases (multi-word lexemes) in the chosen language.
Label of the Wikipedia category name field. Parameter 1 is the Wikipedia language code (for example \'en\'), forming a domain name like en.wikipedia.org; do not translate the domain.
Label above a choice between matching each typed line to Wikidata items or to lexemes.
Option: match each line to Wikidata items (things, places, people, concepts).
Option: match each line to Wikidata lexemes (dictionary entries for words).
Note under the item/lexeme choice. A disambiguation card lets the user pick the right entry when several share the same name.
Label above a choice of how many levels of sub-categories to include.
Option for sub-category depth: do not include any sub-categories.
Option for sub-category depth: two levels. Just the number; localize the digit only if your language uses different digits.
Option for sub-category depth: five levels, which is the maximum allowed.
Note under the sub-category depth choice: categories that contain each other in a loop are detected and not followed again.
Label of a checkbox: whether to also include Wikidata entries that already have a recorded pronunciation.
Explanation under the include-recorded checkbox. P443 is the Wikidata property for pronunciation audio; keep it as is.
Button that fetches and builds the list of words to record from the chosen source.
Headline while each typed line is being looked up on Wikidata.
Explanation while each typed line is being looked up on Wikidata.
Short lowercase progress label while lines are being matched against Wikidata.
Headline while the user\'s SPARQL query is running.
Explanation while the user\'s SPARQL query is running.
Headline while the pages in a Wikipedia category are being collected. \'Walking\' means going through the category and its sub-categories.
Explanation while the pages in a Wikipedia category are being collected.
Small heading on a disambiguation card, for a line that matched several entries. Parameter 1 is the number of this card; parameter 2 is the total number of lines that need a choice.
Explanation on a disambiguation card. Parameter 1 is how many Wikidata items share the label (always 2 or more).
Explanation on a disambiguation card. Parameter 1 is how many lexemes share the spelling (always 2 or more).

Button on a disambiguation card: record every matching entry instead of choosing one. Parameter 1 is how many entries (always 2 or more). The part after the dot means the typed word itself is removed from the list and replaced by those entries.
Small heading: the fourth and last setup step, where the user sees the finished list of words to record.
Short description of the finished list when it came from the user\'s own typed list.
Short description of the finished list when it came from a SPARQL query.
Short description of the finished list when it came from a Wikipedia category.
Small heading of a box suggesting the user check whether list entries already have recordings.
Text of the box suggesting the user check for existing recordings before starting.
Small heading of a box saying the list contains only entries without a recording (\'gaps\' are missing recordings).
Text of the box saying the list contains only entries without a recording.
Small heading of a box saying every entry already has a recording, so new ones will be additional recordings (\'takes\').
Text of the box saying every entry already has a recording.
Short lowercase progress label while checking Wikidata for existing recordings.
Button that checks which list entries already have recordings on Wikidata.
Button that skips the check and uses the list unchanged.
Row label in the check results table; a number is shown next to it. Counts the entries in the list.

Row label in the check results table; a number with a minus sign is shown next to it. Counts entries removed because they already have audio. P443 is the Wikidata pronunciation audio property; keep it as is.
Row label in the check results table; a number with a plus sign is shown next to it. Counts lexeme forms (inflected forms of a word, such as plurals) added because they have no audio yet.
Row label for the total in the check results table; a number is shown next to it. Counts how many entries are left to record.
Big button that starts the recording session. Written in capital letters in English; use capitals only if your script has them.
Small heading when the check found that nothing in the list needs recording.
Small heading when every entry was left out, because it already had a recording or had been skipped earlier.
Headline when every entry was left out, so there is nothing to record.
Explanation when every entry was left out. The quoted text refers to the checkbox label translated in the message \'include_recorded_label\'; keep the two consistent.
Explanation when every entry in the list already has a recording. P443 is the Wikidata pronunciation audio property; keep it as is.
Small lowercase heading of a box with suggestions for finding words that still need recording.
Suggestions for finding words that still need recording.
Button that goes back to choose a different source for the word list.
Button that records the words even though they already have recordings, adding additional recordings (\'second takes\').
Small heading when building the word list failed.
Headline when building the word list failed.
Explanation when building the word list failed.
Warning banner shown above a list when some of the requests used to build it failed.
Progress counter on the recording screen. Parameter 1 is the number of the current word; parameter 2 is the total number of words in the session.
First word of the countdown before recording starts (like \'ready, set, go!\'). Keep it very short.
Second word of the countdown before recording starts (like \'ready, set, go!\'). Keep it very short.
Last word of the countdown before recording starts (like \'ready, set, go!\'). Keep it very short.
Lowercase hint on the recording screen in automatic mode: recording starts by itself when the user starts speaking.

Lowercase hint on the recording screen in automatic mode. Parameter 1 is the number of seconds of silence after which recording stops by itself, with one decimal (for example 1.5). \'s\' is the abbreviation for seconds.
Lowercase hint on the recording screen when the user is recording words again, after marking them for redo during review.
Lowercase status on the recording screen: the microphone is on and waiting for the user to speak.
Lowercase status on the recording screen: the user\'s voice is being recorded.
Lowercase status on the recording screen: recording will stop after a short silence. Parameter 1 is the seconds left, with one decimal. \'s\' is the abbreviation for seconds.
Lowercase status on the recording screen in manual mode, before the user taps Record.
Lowercase hint in manual mode. \'Record\' is the button translated in the message \'recording_manual_record\'; keep them consistent.
Lowercase hint in manual mode while recording. \'Stop\' is the button translated in the message \'recording_manual_stop\'; keep them consistent.
Lowercase hint in manual mode after a word was recorded. \'Next\' and \'Record\' are the buttons translated in \'recording_manual_next\' and \'recording_manual_record\'; keep them consistent.
Banner shown when automatic mode keeps failing to tell when the user starts and stops speaking. Manual mode means the user taps buttons to start and stop.
Button to record the current word again.
Button to skip the current word without recording it.
Button that ends the recording session early.
Label of the toggle when manual mode is on: the user starts and stops each recording with buttons.
Label of the toggle when automatic mode is on: the app starts and stops recording by detecting the voice.
Button in manual mode that starts recording a word.
Button in manual mode that stops recording.
Button in manual mode that moves on to the next word.
Headline shown when the app has no permission to use the microphone.
Explanation shown when the microphone permission is off, reassuring the user about privacy. \'Contribute\' refers to the button that uploads the recordings.
Small lowercase heading above the instructions for turning on the microphone permission.
Path through the Android system settings to the microphone permission. Use the names Android shows in your language for these menus; keep the app name.
Button that opens the Android system settings for this app.
Button that goes back to the word list.
Small lowercase note after recording was interrupted: the half-finished recording was not saved.
Small lowercase heading above the reason the recording was interrupted.
Explanation when recording stopped because a phone call took over the microphone.
Extra warning after an interruption, when the recent recordings had a lot of background noise.
Button to continue recording after an interruption. Parameter 1 is the word the session will continue from.
Lowercase progress counter on the review screen. Parameter 1 is the number of the recording being reviewed; parameter 2 is the total.
Lowercase status on the review screen, before a recording is played back to the user.
Lowercase status on the review screen while the recording is playing.

Lowercase prompt after playback: the user may redo or drop the recording, otherwise it is kept automatically. Parameter 1 is the seconds left to decide, with one decimal. \'s\' is the abbreviation for seconds.
Button that throws away a recording (it will not be uploaded).
Small heading on the summary screen after all words in the session were recorded.
Explanation on the summary screen of how the recordings were processed. Ogg Vorbis is an audio format name; keep it as is. \'s\' is the abbreviation for seconds.
Explanation on the summary screen when no recordings were kept.
Small lowercase heading when there are no recordings to upload.
Suggestion shown when there are no recordings to upload.
Main button on the summary screen: upload the recordings to Wikimedia Commons and link them from Wikidata.
Note about the license the recordings are published under. Creative Commons Zero (CC0) is a license name; use its official name in your language if one exists.
Button that ends the session and deletes the recordings without uploading them.
Button that returns to the first step of setting up a session.
Accessibility label for the button that plays a recording in the summary list.
Accessibility label for the button that records a word in the summary list again.
Title of the confirmation dialog shown before abandoning the session.
Button in the abandon dialog: delete the recordings and exit.
Button in the abandon dialog: cancel and keep the session.
Small tag on a recording in the summary list: the recording is for a Wikidata item (a thing, place, person or concept).
Small tag on a recording in the summary list: the recording is for a lexeme form (one inflected form of a word, such as a plural).

plurals.name: summary_headline_ready
plurals.item: Headline on the summary screen. The number of recordings is shown separately, in a very large font, just before this text, and chooses the plural form. Shown when the recordings are ready to upload.

plurals.name: summary_headline_kept
plurals.item: Headline on the summary screen. The number of recordings is shown separately, in a very large font, just before this text, and chooses the plural form. Shown when the session ended without any recordings to upload.

plurals.name: summary_abandon_dialog_body
plurals.item: Body of the confirmation dialog shown before abandoning the session. Parameter 1 is the number of recordings that will be deleted.

resources.string: Small heading on the upload screen while recordings are being uploaded.
Progress text on the upload screen. The number of recordings already uploaded is shown separately, in a large font, just before this text. Parameter 1 is the total number of recordings.
Small lowercase label above the recording currently being uploaded.
Lowercase progress step for the current upload: the audio file was uploaded to Wikimedia Commons.
Lowercase progress step for the current upload: categories were added to the file on Commons.

Lowercase progress step for the current upload: a pronunciation audio statement (Wikidata property P443) was added. Parameter 1 is the Wikidata identifier of the item or lexeme form (for example Q42 or L1-F1). Keep P443 as is.
Note on the upload screen, explaining that uploads continue in the background while the app is open.
Banner on the upload screen when the internet connection is lost.
Small lowercase heading above the list of uploads that failed and need the user to act.
Short lowercase status tag on a failed upload: the app is trying again.
Short lowercase status tag on a failed upload: a file with the same name already exists on Commons.
Short lowercase status tag on a failed upload: waiting before trying again.
Error shown when uploading a file to Commons failed. Parameter 1 is the error description, which may be in English.
Error shown when adding the pronunciation statement (Wikidata property P443) failed. Parameter 1 is the error description, which may be in English. Keep P443 as is.
Button on an upload that failed because the file name is taken: upload it again under a different name.
Button on a failed upload: delete this recording and do not upload it.
Button: stop trying the failed uploads for now and keep them on the device.
Note explaining what happens to recordings left for later.

plurals.name: contribution_retry_all_now
plurals.item: Button that retries all failed uploads at once. Parameter 1 is the number of failed uploads.

resources.string: Explanation on the final screen after every recording was uploaded and linked. P443 is the Wikidata pronunciation audio property; keep it as is.
Link that opens the user\'s list of uploads on Wikimedia Commons.
Link that opens the user\'s list of edits (contributions) on Wikidata.
Button that starts a new session with a different word list.

plurals.name: done_headline
plurals.item: Headline on the final screen. Parameter 1 is the number of recordings that are now published and playable on Wikidata.

plurals.name: done_explainer_partial
plurals.item: Explanation on the final screen when some uploads did not finish. Parameter 1 is the number of recordings that were not uploaded.

resources.string: Title of the Settings screen.
Title of a setting: skip the profile-selection step and use the most recently used speaker profile.
Explanation of the auto-use-last-profile setting. Step 1 is choosing a speaker profile.
Title of a setting: cut silence off the start and end of each recording.
Explanation of the trim-silence setting. Ogg Vorbis is an audio format name; keep it as is. \'s\' is the abbreviation for seconds.
Label of the setting for the language of the app\'s interface (the language of these messages).
Note under the interface language setting. translatewiki.net is a website name; keep it as is.
Label of the setting for how long a silence ends a recording in automatic mode. It is followed by a slider showing a number of seconds.
Value next to the silence slider: a number of seconds with one decimal (for example 1.5). \'s\' is the abbreviation for seconds.
Label of the setting for the largest number of entries a word list may contain.
Explanation of the maximum list size setting. LIMIT is a SPARQL keyword and must not be translated.
Label of the section about words the user skipped during recording.
Explanation of what happens to skipped words and what forgetting them does.
Label of the account section in Settings.
Button that logs the user out. Parameter 1 is the Wikimedia username.
Button that leaves Settings and returns to the recording session.
Title of the statistics screen.
Lowercase label under a large number on the statistics screen: the total number of recordings the user made.
Lowercase label under a large number on the statistics screen: how many recordings were for Wikidata items.
Lowercase label under a large number on the statistics screen: how many recordings were for lexeme forms (inflected forms of words).
Column heading in the statistics table: the month.
Column heading in the statistics table: number of recordings for Wikidata items.
Column heading in the statistics table: number of recordings for lexeme forms.
Column heading in the statistics table: total number of recordings (items and forms together).
Heading of the statistics section for years before the current one.
Line on the About screen. Parameter 1 is the app version number. Apache-2.0 is the license name and CREDITS is a file name; keep both as they are.
Description of the app on the About screen. Lingua Libre and LinguaRecorder are names of other projects; keep them as they are.
Heading of the credits section on the About screen.
Closing note on the About screen about licensing and privacy.

plurals.name: settings_forget_skipped_button
plurals.item: Button in Settings that clears the list of skipped words so they can appear in lists again. Parameter 1 is the number of skipped words.

plurals.name: interrupted_stop_review
plurals.item: Button after an interruption: end recording and go to review. Parameter 1 is the number of recordings (\'takes\') made so far.

plurals.name: list_entries_found_count
plurals.item: Count shown above the finished word list. Parameter 1 is the number of entries in the list.

plurals.name: list_filtered_already_recorded
plurals.item: Note above the word list. Parameter 1 is the number of entries left out because they already have a recording.

plurals.name: list_filtered_previously_skipped
plurals.item: Note above the word list. Parameter 1 is the number of entries left out because the user skipped them in earlier sessions.

plurals.name: empty_title
plurals.item: Headline when every entry in the list already has a recording. Parameter 1 is the number of entries.

plurals.name: profile_recordings_count
plurals.item: Line on a speaker profile card. Parameter 1 is how many recordings this profile has made.
